admissionRule: Admitted when calibration has been measured on every task. Passing is not required. The verdict travels with the entry and every recommendation must carry it.

entries.summary: Neural posterior estimation with a masked autoregressive flow. The default choice in most simulation based inference pipelines.

measurements.why: Accuracy on this task spans only 0.064 R2 across all eight entries, so accuracy alone does not distinguish this one. NPE is amortized: it learns the posterior directly, so inference is a single forward pass and costs almost nothing per observation. CAMELS uses a 25 Mpc/h box, only about three times the 8 Mpc/h scale sigma_8 is defined on, so sample variance on that scale is large and sigma_8 recovers poorly. Coverage at 68 per cent is 0.569 against a nominal 0.680, so the posterior is too narrow. Single density estimators are known to be overconfident (Hermans et al. 2022).

Single density estimators are known to be overconfident (Hermans et al. 2022).

failureModes: MEASURED overconfident on all three CAMELS tasks: mean coverage at the 68 per cent level is 0.595 against a nominal 0.680, which is 7.8 sigma low. Error bars from this entry are too small.
Single density estimators tend to be overconfident (Hermans et al. 2022), which is the dangerous direction because error bars come out too small.
Autoregressive structure imposes a parameter ordering, so strongly degenerate parameters can be harder to capture than with a spline flow.

entries.summary: Neural likelihood estimation with a MAF. Learns p(x|theta), so the prior can be changed after training without retraining.

measurements.why: Accuracy on this task spans only 0.064 R2 across all eight entries, so accuracy alone does not distinguish this one. NLE learns a proxy rather than the posterior, so every observation needs its own MCMC run. That is why inference takes 3289 s here against under 3 s for NPE. CAMELS uses a 25 Mpc/h box, only about three times the 8 Mpc/h scale sigma_8 is defined on, so sample variance on that scale is large and sigma_8 recovers poorly. Coverage at 68 per cent is 0.540 against a nominal 0.680, so the posterior is too narrow. Single density estimators are known to be overconfident (Hermans et al. 2022).
